data.narrative:
Hermeus, a Series C-stage developer of supersonic and hypersonic aircraft, carries a current post-money valuation of $1.0B following $500M in total capital raised. The supersonic and hypersonic sector comprises a sparse peer set: two public comparables (DRSHF and IDEAFORGE.NS) and one identified private peer (Boom Supersonic). The narrowness of this universe constrains traditional peer-based valuation approaches.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable triangulation lens. Applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier—standard for Series C progression to the subsequent financing round—to Hermeus's $1.0B post-money valuation yields $1.7B. Peer-median analysis could not be reliably applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the supersonic and hypersonic sector; a single private peer and two public companies do not meet the minimum threshold of three datapoints required for robust median calculation without introducing sector-wide noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B to $2.0B, with a central estimate of $1.7B. This range reflects stage-appropriate expansion assumptions rather than material operational leverage or de-risking. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-sector peers at similar funding stages, regulatory pathway clarity for commercial supersonic operations, and the nascent nature of hypersonic commercialization timelines. The single-method foundation of this estimate underscores the need for updated peer data or direct customer/revenue metrics to strengthen conviction.
